entities.summary: Andrea da Segni was a prominent Italian Franciscan friar born as a member of the noble house of Conti di Segni around 1240. He studied at the University of Rome and later became a professor of theology at the same institution. Da Segni was a key figure in the development of the Franciscan Order's spirituality and was particularly influential in the formation of the Rule of St. Francis. His teachings emphasized the importance of poverty, chastity, and obedience, and he was known for his piety and humility. Da Segni died on February 1, 1302, at the age of 62, leaving behind a legacy that continued to shape Franciscan thought and practice for centuries to come. He is remembered as a champion of social justice and a defender of the poor, and his feast day is celebrated on January 30. Da Segni's writings, including his commentary on the Rule of St. Francis, remain an important source of inspiration for Franciscan scholars and spiritual seekers today.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Andrea da Segni was a key figure in the development of Franciscan spirituality, whose teachings emphasized the importance of poverty, chastity, and obedience. His legacy continued to shape Franciscan thought and practice for centuries to come.
